title: On Distinguishing the two plants by the leaf
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：distinguish　|　正文 367 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 distinguish 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the fisherman ① distinguished the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② distinguishes the two plants by the leaf without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ distinguish the two plants by the leaf at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ distinguished the two plants by the leaf before — a line in the logbook for July 1981 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Distinguishing the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ distinguish himself in the final race without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Distinguish himself in the final race at once and never mention it again.

By 1994 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ distinguishes himself in the final race for the whole place every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ distinguished the two plants by the leaf again when nobody else would.

⑩ To distinguish the two plants by the leaf, my mother said in 1999, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody distinguishes the two plants by the leaf without a word of thanks again and somebody must distinguish the two plants by the leaf for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 区分（一般过去式 distinguished the two plants by the leaf：1987 年渔人头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 区分（一般现在 distinguishes the two plants by the leaf：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 区分（不定式 to distinguish the two plants by the leaf：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 区分（过去完成时 had distinguished the two plants by the leaf：1981 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 区分（动名词 distinguishing the two plants by the leaf 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 使出众（distinguish himself in the final race：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去使出众在最后那场赛跑里出人头地）
G. v. 使出众（distinguish himself in the final race：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 区分（后段两处：新来的船工照例 distinguishes himself in the final race，而母亲又一次 distinguished the two plants by the leaf）

distinguish 意为“区分”，自那以后渔人不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 distinguishes。
distinguish 意为“区分”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯区分靠叶子区分那两种植物”，此处为不定式 to distinguish the two plants by the leaf。
distinguish 意为“区分”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1994 年之前就有人区分过，故用过去完成时 had distinguished。
distinguish 意为“区分”，渔人说“区分靠叶子区分那两种植物这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 distinguishing the two plants by the leaf 作主语。
distinguish 意为“使出众”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去使出众在最后那场赛跑里出人头地”，should ever 之后用原形 distinguish himself in the final race。
distinguish 意为“使出众”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻使出众在最后那场赛跑里出人头地（distinguish himself in the final race at once），以后再也不要提起。
distinguish 意为“区分”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例使出众在最后那场赛跑里出人头地，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 distinguishes。
distinguish 意为“区分”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人区分靠叶子区分那两种植物，用一般过去式 distinguished 叙述。
distinguish 意为“区分”，结尾那句是母亲 1999 年的话：要区分靠叶子区分那两种植物，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

items: 1987 年，渔人替所有人区分靠叶子区分那两种植物；渔港里每一个船工都说这是头一回。（distinguished the two plants by the leaf）

老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻使出众在最后那场赛跑里出人头地，以后再也不要提起。（distinguish himself in the final race，祈使句）
answers: In 1987 the fisherman distinguished the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three seasons on, the fisherman still distinguishes the two plants by the leaf without a word of thanks without being asked.
My mother said later that to distinguish the two plants by the leaf at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had distinguished the two plants by the leaf long before 1994, and the line in the logbook for July proves it.
Distinguishing the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 distinguish 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the fisherman distinguished the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman distinguishes the two plants by the leaf without a word of thanks whenever the harbour asks.
Distinguishing the two plants by the leaf for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever distinguish himself in the final race without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour distinguishes himself in the final race for the whole place every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother distinguished the two plants by the leaf again, and the harbour remembered that half.
